meta.what: Places where this corpus contradicts itself about a matter of fact.
meta.why: PANTHEON_VISION Non-Negotiable 2 asks that contradiction and competing interpretations be preserved. Nothing measured whether they are, because there was no set of questions whose correct answer is 'both'. A question here is answered correctly only if the Constellation carries an entity from BOTH sides; carrying one side and not the other is the encyclopaedia behaviour the Chronik is supposed to refuse.
meta.how: Each side was located in the file by line number and its sentence quoted exactly. Only contradictions verifiable in this corpus are listed: Works and Days is not in this edition, so the Pandora and races-of-men contrasts that the ticket guessed at do not exist here.
meta.note: `expect` names are the entities that should reach the Constellation for that side, spelled as the translation spells them. Sides A and B are not ordered by correctness — neither is wrong, and the substrate is not asked to choose.

sides.label: Night, without a father
sides.evidence: Also she bare the Destinies and ruthless avenging Fates, Clotho and Lachesis and Atropos

sides.label: Themis, to Zeus
sides.evidence: Next he married bright Themis who bare ... the Moerae (Fates) to whom wise Zeus gave the greatest honour

questions.question: Who was the mother of Asclepius?

sides.label: Arsinoe
sides.evidence: And Arsinoe was joined with the son of Zeus and Leto and bare a son Asclepius

sides.label: Coronis
sides.evidence: In the Dotian plain fair Coronis, daughter of King Phlegyas, bare him

questions.corpus_flags_it: line 1433: 'Some say (Asclepius) was the son of Arsinoe, others of Coronis.'

questions.question: Who was the mother of Helen?

sides.label: a daughter of Ocean
sides.evidence: Hesiod, however, makes Helen the child neither of Leda nor Nemesis, but daughter of Ocean and Zeus.

sides.label: Nemesis
sides.evidence: Rich-tressed Nemesis once gave her birth when she had been joined in love with Zeus

questions.corpus_flags_it: line 1455 names and rejects both rival mothers.

sides.label: Earth, by Tartarus
sides.evidence: huge Earth bare her youngest child Typhoeus of the love of Tartarus

sides.label: Hera, alone and angry
sides.work: Hymn III to Pythian Apollo ll. 305-306
sides.evidence: Once on a time Hera bare him because she was angry with father Zeus

questions.question: Whose daughter is Nemesis?

sides.label: Night, without a father
sides.evidence: Also deadly Night bare Nemesis (Indignation) to afflict mortal men

sides.label: Zeus
sides.evidence: Nemesis tried to escape him and liked not to lie in love with her father Zeus

questions.note: In the Theogony's chronology Zeus is not yet born when Night bears Nemesis.

questions.question: How was Aphrodite born?

sides.label: from the foam of Heaven's severed members
sides.evidence: a white foam spread around them from the immortal flesh, and in it there grew a maiden

sides.label: daughter of Zeus
sides.evidence: Aphrodite, the daughter of Zeus stood before him

questions.note: Hymn VI (line 4537) backs the Theogony against Hymn V: two adjacent hymns to one goddess disagree. Side B is marked only by Zeus, who is everywhere in this corpus, so this question is the weakest of the seven to measure with.

questions.question: Did Hephaestus have a father?

sides.label: Hera alone, without Zeus
sides.evidence: But Hera without union with Zeus—for she was very angry and quarrelled with her mate—bare famous Hephaestus

sides.label: Zeus is his father
sides.evidence: worked with his own hands as a favour to Zeus his father

questions.note: Side B is marked only by Zeus; see the note on aphrodite-birth.
